name: Engineering: Ladder
description: Ten levels of one engineering job: build a small in-memory database (a mini Redis) from a written specification, checked by hidden unit tests. Level 1 is three commands (SET, GET, DEL); every level adds commands and rules on top of all the earlier ones (counting and bulk loading, exact big-integer arithmetic, nested transactions, ordered scans, expiry with a clock, renames, snapshots, bulk deletes, range counts) and larger hidden inputs, up to 200,000 keys. The top levels need every rule right in every combination AND the efficient design: copying the store, scanning every key or re-sorting on each command runs out of time. Expected replies come from a reference solution and are re-checked by two independent implementations.
hook: Build a database one feature at a time: how far up does it get before something breaks?
author: Gauntlet Ladders

cases.prompt:
Write a JavaScript function `runStore(commands)` that simulates a small in-memory key-value store (a mini database) and returns its replies.

`commands` is an array of commands, processed in order. Each command is an array of strings: the command name followed by its arguments, for example `["SET", "user:1", "Ada"]`. The function returns an array of strings with exactly one reply per command, in the same order.

- A **key** is a non-empty string of at most 24 characters, each one of `a`-`z`, `0`-`9`, `:` and `_`.
- A **value** is a string of at most 24 printable ASCII characters (character codes 32 to 126, so spaces and punctuation are allowed). A value may be the empty string.
- A key **exists** once a value is stored under it, until it is removed.
- Every command is well-formed: it is one of the commands listed below, with exactly the arguments shown, each of the stated form.

The commands, level by level (this task is level 1; all of it applies):

**Level 1: basic commands**
- `["SET", key, value]`: stores `value` under `key`, replacing any value it had. Reply `"OK"`.
- `["GET", key]`: reply the value stored under `key`, or `"(nil)"` if the key does not exist.
- `["DEL", key]`: removes the key. Reply `"1"` if it existed, `"0"` if it did not.

**Size of the tests.** A test has at most 200 commands. The hidden tests include the largest sizes, so every command should take time that grows at most slowly with the size of the store.

Examples:
```javascript
runStore([["SET","user:1","Ada"],["GET","user:1"],["GET","user:2"],["DEL","user:1"],["DEL","user:1"],["GET","user:1"]])
// returns ["OK","Ada","(nil)","1","0","(nil)"]
```
